title: aiBytes edition
description: One day's curated edition: content/editions/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Written by the curate step from the raw source snapshots, committed, and served as static JSON. Consumers are the aiBytes_ web app, the Chrome extension, and the weekly newsletter skill. A shipped extension cannot be hotfixed, so this contract is append-only: add fields, never rename or remove them, and bump schema_version for anything breaking. Keys are snake_case throughout, following the shape in the product spec.

schema_version.description: Bumped only for a breaking change. Consumers must refuse a version they do not know rather than guess.

date.description: The edition date, and the file's name. One edition per day; a missed day has no file and the edition bar shows the gap rather than a fake edition.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the curate run. Drives the edition bar's 'updated 4h ago'.

counts.description: Visible items per category. Excludes hidden items, because the app skips those - so hide.py must decrement here too. All four v1 categories are always present, even at zero, so consumers never branch on undefined.

items.description: Every item that passed the relevance filter - there is no per-category cap, the filter is the editorial line. Written in category order (launches, repos, news, hn) then by rank within the category, so a re-run diffs cleanly; consumers re-sort for their own views rather than relying on it. Rejected items and their reasons go to rejected.json, not here.

id.description: Stable id, unique within the edition and globally: <source-prefix>-<slug>-<edition date>, e.g. ph-chatcut-2026-08-27. The date suffix must equal this edition's date - that is what makes saves (item_id + edition_date) resolvable and catches an item copied forward from yesterday.

title.description: Links to `url`, which for a product or article is the destination rather than the source page.

summary.description: One line, written by the curate step in Ledger's voice: plain, factual, no hype. Capped so it stays two lines on a card.

url.description: Where the title links: the product site, the article, the repo.

source.description: The fetcher that produced the item. Matches a source module's NAME in packages/fetchers, which the tests assert. Drives the card's image rules and mark fallback.

source_url.description: The source page the source name links to: the PH page, the HN thread, the GitHub repo. Equal to `url` where the source is the destination (TechCrunch, and GitHub or HN when the item is the thing itself). Always present so the UI never has to fall back.

category.description: Exactly one per item; the primary filter chip and the section heading. Show HN stories are launches, not hn. The v1.1 categories (discussions, releases, research) are deliberately absent - adding one is a conscious change here, in counts, and in every consumer's chip list.

tags.description: Zero to four, drawn only from the display names in tags.json - never free-form, or the filter stops being clean. The list is not enumerated here on purpose: tags.json is the single source and can grow without a schema change. validate.py cross-checks membership when it is given the tag list.

signals.description: Present only when the source reports something. Rendered in this order: upvotes or points, stars gained, comments. Omitted entirely rather than emitted empty, so a re-run diffs cleanly.

comments.description: Comment count on the source page.

stars_gained.description: GitHub stars gained over the window.

meta.description: Small per-source extras the card meta row shows. A locked set rather than a free bucket: adding a field is a deliberate edit here, which is the point of a contract. Omit a key rather than writing null, and omit the object entirely rather than emitting it empty, so a re-run diffs cleanly.

language.description: GitHub repo language; shown as a dot plus name.

reading_time.description: TechCrunch reading time, as the source phrases it.

published_at.description: When the source published it. Absent for GitHub trending, which has no publish date - so consumers must not sort on it alone.

hidden.description: Always written, even as false, so hide.py flips one line and the commit reads clearly. The site and the newsletter both skip hidden items, and counts excludes them.

rank.description: The item's place in the edition's one reading order across every source, 1 first. Optional, because editions written before it existed have none - but all or none: when any item has a rank, every item does, and the ranks are exactly 1..N over all items, hidden ones included, so hiding never renumbers. Consumers sort ascending and must not assume the visible ranks are contiguous. Independent of the items' order in the file, which stays grouped by category.

image.description: The 40px card image. `type` picks the treatment: logo is rounded (Product Hunt), avatar is a circle (GitHub owner), thumbnail is cropped square (TechCrunch og:image), none means the source mark fills the slot instead (Hacker News). Every type keeps the same footprint so cards align.
